q: 1. In measuring horizontal angles, the theodolite should be turned
options: clockwise from the forward station to the back station
clockwise from the back station to the forward station
anticlockwise from the forward station to the back station
anticlockwise from the back station to the forward station
explain: Standard practice for measuring horizontal angles is to turn the theodolite clockwise, starting from the back station reading and swinging to the forward station.

q: 2. The theodolite is an instrument used for measuring very accurately
explain: A theodolite is the primary precision instrument used for accurately measuring both horizontal and vertical angles.

q: 3. The process of turning the telescope of a theodolite over its supporting axis through 180 in a vertical plane, is called
explain: This action - rotating the telescope through 180 degrees over the horizontal (trunnion) axis - is known by any of the equivalent terms: transiting, reversing, or plunging.

q: 4. In any closed traverse, if the survey work is correct, then
options: the algebraic sum of latitudes should be equal to zero
the algebraic sum of departures should be equal to zero
the sum of northings should be equal to the sum of southings
explain: For a correctly closed traverse, the algebraic sum of latitudes and departures must each equal zero, which also implies the sum of northings equals the sum of southings - so all of the above are valid consequences.

q: 5. The latitude and departure of a traverse line are both positive when the whole circle bearing of the line lies in the
explain: For a WCB in the first quadrant (0-90 degrees, north-east direction), both the latitude (northward) and departure (eastward) components are positive.

q: 6. When the latitudes and departures are so adjusted that the algebraic sum of the latitudes and departures are equal to zero, the operation is called
explain: This overall adjustment process, applied to both latitudes and departures to remove closing error, is known as balancing the traverse.

q: 7. When the angular and linear measurements are equally precise in traversing, the balancing of a traverse in done by
explain: Bowditch's rule (compass rule) is used to balance a traverse when both angular and linear measurements are considered equally precise, distributing error in proportion to the length of each leg.

q: 8. An angle made by a survey line with the prolongation of the proceeding line, is known as
explain: This angle, formed between a survey line and the prolongation (extension) of the previous line, is by definition the deflection angle.

q: 9. A deflection angle in a traverse is equal to the
options: difference between the included angle and 180
difference between 360 and the included and 180
sum of the included angel and 180
explain: A deflection angle is computed as the difference between the included angle at a station and 180 degrees, representing the deviation from a straight continuation of the previous line.

q: 10. The direct angles may have any value between
explain: Direct angles (measured directly in the field between two lines at a station, typically clockwise from the previous station) may range anywhere from 0 to 360 degrees.

q: 11. The line of sight is kept as high above ground surface as possible to minimize the error in the observed angles due to
explain: Keeping the line of sight well above the ground reduces the error caused by both shimmering (heat haze) and horizontal refraction near the ground surface, both of which distort observed angles.

q: 12. The distance between terminal points computed from known, as
explain: The distance between terminal points, once computed from known data, may be referred to by any of these equivalent terms - traverse leg, base, or traverse base - depending on context, so all of the above apply.

q: 13. To avoid large centering error with very short legs, observations are generally made
options: by using optical system for centering the theodolite
to a target fixed on theodolite tripod on which theodolite may be fitted easily
explain: To minimize centering errors on short traverse legs, any of these techniques may be applied together - sighting to chain pins, using optical centering systems, or using targets fixed on the tripod - so all of the above apply.

q: 14. When internal angles are to be subtended by a thedolite survey for closed traverse
options: exterior angles are measures when the traverse goes anti-clockwise
explain: For internal angles to be correctly measured and used in a closed theodolite traverse, the traverse should be run in a counter-clockwise direction.

q: 15. When the first object is to be focused, the scale is set to 0 00'00 and then
options: the upper screw is fixed, lower screw released, the object sighted, lower screw fixed and lower tangent screw operated
both the clamp screw fixed, top tangent screw operated
bottom clamp screw fixed, top screw released, object sighted and upper tangent screw operated
object is exactly bisected by operating both the upper and lower tangent screws whichever is convenient
explain: To focus on the first object with the scale set at zero, the lower (bottom) clamp screw is fixed and the upper screw is released to sight the object, then the upper tangent screw is used for fine adjustment.

q: 16. Resolving power of a telescope depends on
options: the pupil aperture of the eye
the diameter of the object glass
explain: The resolving power of a telescope primarily depends on the diameter (aperture) of the object glass (objective lens); a larger objective diameter gives better resolving power.

q: 17. While rotating the theodolite in the horizontal plane, the bubble of the bubble tube takes the same position in its tube, it indicates
options: the line of collimation is perpendicular to vertical axis
explain: If the bubble remains centred (same position) throughout a full horizontal rotation of the theodolite, it indicates that the vertical (rotation) axis is truly vertical.

q: 18. Can the vertical axis coincide with any other axis in any position of telescope?
options: Yes, with the geometric centre of level head
Yes, with the axis of altitude levels
explain: The vertical axis is a fixed reference axis distinct from the trunnion axis and line of collimation, and it is not possible for it to coincide with any other axis in any telescope position.

q: 19. For a transit theodolite the least reading on the main scale is 20'. If its vernier scale should read 20, then
options: 59 on the main scale are divided into 60 equal parts
20 on the main scale are divided into 60 equal divisions
19 40' on the main scale are divided into 60 equal parts
20 20' on the main scale are divided into 60 equal parts
explain: To achieve a vernier least count of 20 seconds from a main scale division of 20 minutes, 59 main scale divisions (equivalent to 19 40') are divided into 60 equal parts on the vernier.

q: 20. For a closed traverse the omitted measurements may be calculated
options: length or bearing of adjacent side
explain: For a closed traverse with one measurement omitted, computation can determine any missing quantity - length only, bearing only, or both length and bearing of an adjacent side - so all of the above are valid, depending on which data is missing.

q: 21. The length of a traverse line (L) may be obtained by
options: L = Latitude x Secant of reduced bearing
L = Departure x Cosecant of reduced bearing
explain: All three formulas given are mathematically equivalent ways of computing the length of a traverse line from its latitude, departure, and reduced bearing - so any one of the above can be used.

q: 22. In a closed traverse the algebraic sum of deflection angle is
explain: For a closed traverse, the algebraic sum of all deflection angles (right deflections positive, left negative) must equal 360 degrees, corresponding to one complete traverse around the figure.

q: 23. In a precision traverse, included angles are measured by setting the vernier
options: to read zero exactly on back station
to read 5 exactly on back station
somewhere near zero and reading both verniers on back station
explain: In precision traversing, included angles are measured by setting the vernier to somewhere near (not exactly) zero when backsighted, and reading both verniers to average out eccentricity errors.
